after_snippet:
# In pytest 9.0.0, CI mode only activates with non-empty values

import subprocess
import sys
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    tmp = Path(tmpdir)
    (tmp / "test_x.py").write_text("def test_x(): pass")
    
    # In 9.0.0, empty string does not activate CI mode
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["CI"] = ""  # Empty value - does NOT activate CI mode in 9.0.0
    
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", tmp / "test_x.py"],
        cwd=tmp,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True
    )
    # To activate CI mode, set a non-empty value
    assert result.returncode == 0
    
    # To activate CI mode in 9.0.0, use non-empty value
    env["CI"] = "true"
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", tmp / "test_x.py"],
        cwd=tmp,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0
before_snippet:
# In pytest 8.4.2, CI/CD mode would activate if $CI or $BUILD_NUMBER were defined,
# even if set to empty string

import subprocess
import sys
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    tmp = Path(tmpdir)
    (tmp / "test_x.py").write_text("def test_x(): pass")
    
    # In 8.4.2, setting CI to empty string would still activate CI mode
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["CI"] = ""  # Empty value
    
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--collect-only", tmp / "test_x.py"],
        cwd=tmp,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True
    )
    # In 8.4.2 this would have CI mode active
    assert result.returncode == 0
title: CI mode only activates with non-empty CI or BUILD_NUMBER environment variables
